title: AI Knowledge Management and Content Governance

questions.question: Why do AI assistants need governed knowledge sources?
options: Because retrieval can make stale or wrong sources look authoritative
Because content owners are never needed
Because access rules should be ignored
questions.explanation: Source governance protects trust in AI-assisted answers.

questions.question: Which signal is part of this lesson?
questions.explanation: Stale content is a core knowledge-source risk.

questions.question: What does the Python artifact produce?
questions.explanation: The artifact ranks source risks and recommends controls.

questions.question: Which control belongs to this lesson?
questions.explanation: Freshness checks help decide whether content is AI-ready.

questions.question: When should content be cleaned up before AI use?
options: When content is stale, duplicated, ownerless, or access-sensitive
Only when no one uses it
Only when it is already reviewed
questions.explanation: These signals can make AI answers unreliable or unsafe.

questions.question: What should every important knowledge source have?
options: Owner, freshness check, source rank, and access rule
questions.explanation: These controls make knowledge sources ready for AI assistants.
